subtitle: A Rajput widow walks out of the fort and into song

panels.shot: wide, dusk-lit fort rampart with solitary figure silhouetted against a vast sky
panels.action: Mirabai stands alone on a Chittor-like rampart, veena cradled in her arms, looking out toward a hazy horizon where temples and faraway villages glow faintly.

dialogue.text: Between Rajput law and Krishna’s love, Mirabai of Merta chose a path so fierce that history itself falls into song and silence.

i18n.hi: राजपूत नियम और कृष्ण प्रेम के बीच, मेड़ता की मीरा ने ऐसी राह चुनी कि इतिहास खुद गीत और सन्नाटे में बदल गया

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of Rajasthan landscape into a small fortified town
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of arid hills, scattered khejri trees and a modest fort at Kudki or Merta, with a child Mirabai watching a wedding procession from an inner courtyard balcony.

dialogue.text: The record is thin: no signature, no royal farman. Yet across Rajasthan, people still point and say, ‘Here lived Mira of Merta.’

i18n.hi: दस्तावेज़ कम हैं: न हस्ताक्षर, न शाही फ़रमान। पर राजस्तान भर में लोग आज भी इशारा करके कहते हैं, ‘यहाँ रहती थी मेड़ता की मीरा।’

panels.shot: gentle close-up on young Mirabai’s face, eyes fixed on an image of Krishna
panels.action: Young Mirabai sits in a shaded verandah, holding a small painted image of Krishna, her eyes wide with absorbed devotion as sounds of drums and talk drift faintly from the courtyard.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers say the girl of Kudki loved Krishna as her bridegroom. The historian nods, but notes: our first written trace comes half a century after she was gone.

i18n.hi: बाद की कहानियाँ कहती हैं: कुड़की की लड़की ने कृष्ण को अपना दूल्हा माना। इतिहासकार मानता है, पर याद दिलाता है: पहला लिखित निशान आधी सदी बाद मिलता है

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Rajput wedding hall, with focus on Mira among the ritual crowd
panels.action: A teenage Mirabai, richly dressed in Rajput bridal finery, sits near a ceremonial fire, elders around her performing marriage rites in a Mewar-style palace hall.

dialogue.text: What most scholars can still agree on is this: Mira was born into a Rathore branch at Merta and married into the Sisodia house of Mewar.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादातर विद्वान इतना मानते हैं: मीरा मेड़ता की राठौड़ शाख में जन्मी, और मेवाड़ की सिसोदिया रियासत में ब्याही गई

panels.shot: wide shot of Chittor fort interior, showing palatial quarters and a small shrine
panels.action: Mirabai walks through Chittor’s inner palace, past armed retainers and noblewomen; her steps slow as she turns into a private shrine where a Krishna murti stands garlanded.

dialogue.text: Inside Chittor’s high walls, she entered the tight world of Rajput honor: purdah, clan politics, and the quiet inner shrines where women made their own vows.

i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ की ऊँची दीवारों के भीतर वो पहुँची राजपूती मान की तंग दुनिया में: परदा, कुल की सियासत, और वो शांत मंदिर जहाँ औरतें अपनी मनौती माँगती थीं

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Mira seated before the deity, hands folded, veena resting nearby
panels.action: Mirabai kneels before a Krishna idol, eyes closed, lips moving in soft, unheard words, with a veena by her side and oil lamps flickering around.

dialogue.text: In those shrines, later singers place the first bhajans. But when we search old manuscripts, only a small, hard core can be safely tied to her name.

i18n.hi: उन्हीं मंदिरों में, गीतकार पहली भजनों को रखते हैं। पर जब हम पुराने ग्रंथ टटोलते हैं, तो सिर्फ़ थोड़े से कड़े गीत हैं जिन्हें भरोसे से उसके नाम से जोड़ सकते हैं

panels.shot: medium shot of palace women discussing, Mira slightly apart, absorbed in song
panels.action: In a marble-pillared women’s courtyard, Rajput ladies sit in conversation, while Mirabai sits a little away, eyes distant, fingers poised on veena strings.

panels.shot: low-angle corridor shot, Mira walking past stern elder figures, tension in the air
panels.action: Mirabai walks through a dim corridor, facing two stern older male relatives in courtly dress; their bodies rigid, hers upright but composed, a veena held firmly in her hand.

dialogue.text: Soon, stories say, her devotion clashed with marital duty. Modern scholars read these tales against Mewar’s own crises, where a widow’s silence guarded family honor.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही, कथाएँ बताती हैं, उसका भक्ति-पथ ससुराल के फ़र्ज़ से टकराया। आधुनिक विद्वान इन किस्सों को मेवाड़ की उन मुश्किल घड़ियों से जोड़कर पढ़ते हैं, जहाँ विधवा की चुप्पी से ही कुल इज़्ज़त बचती थी

panels.shot: somber close-up, Mira in simple widow’s white, looking straight ahead
panels.action: Mirabai, now in pale widow’s clothing without ornaments, sits on a low stool in a sparse room, her gaze steady, hands loosely folded over her lap.

dialogue.text: Whether or not each detail of the hagiographies is true, they agree on one bold contour: as widow, Mira broke Rajput codes that demanded withdrawal and quiet.

i18n.hi: चाहे हागियोग्राफ़ी की हर बात सच हो या नहीं, सब एक तेज रेखा पर सहमत हैं: विधवा होते हुए मीरा ने उन राजपूती नियमों को तोड़ा जो उसे ओट और ख़ामोशी में गायब होने को कहते थे

panels.shot: wide courtyard shot, Mira descending steps toward a temple filled with commoners
panels.action: Mirabai walks down stone steps from the palace toward a Krishna temple thronged with townspeople—artisans, farmers, women with brass pots—who glance up as she approaches.

dialogue.text: Instead of staying behind screens, tradition remembers her walking to temples, mingling with craftsmen, singers, servants—crossing the invisible lines of caste and rank.

i18n.hi: परदों में छिपने के बजाय, परंपरा उसे याद करती है मंदिरों तक जाते हुए, कारीगरों, गायकों, नौकरों के बीच घुलते हुए—जात और दर्जे की अदृश्य रेखाएँ पार करते हुए

panels.shot: medium shot inside a temple hall, Mira leading a small kirtan circle
panels.action: Mirabai stands near the deity in a temple hall, softly playing the veena and singing; a mixed group of devotees sit around her, listening with rapt faces.

dialogue.text: Bhaktamala, around 1600, names her among Krishna’s lovers and singers, already a legend. Yet this first written portrait arrives decades after the living woman had passed.

i18n.hi: भक्तमाला, करीब 1600, उसे कृष्ण के प्रेमियों और गायकों में गिनती है, तब तक बन चुकी दास्तान। पर यह पहला लिखित चित्र उस ज़िंदा स्त्री के जाने के कई दशक बाद आता है

panels.shot: slow push-in on a palm-leaf manuscript being copied by a scribe, Mira’s imagined figure faintly superimposed
panels.action: A scribe in early 17th-century attire bends over palm leaves, copying verses about Mira as a faint, ghostlike image of Mirabai singing appears behind him.

dialogue.text: Priyadas, a century later, expanded Nabhadas’ notes into vivid episodes—poison cups, snakes, miracles—shaping how millions would picture Mirabai thereafter.

i18n.hi: एक सदी बाद, प्रियदास ने नाभदास की झलकियों को फैलाकर ज़िंदा क़िस्से बनाए—ज़हर का प्याला, साँप, चमत्कार—जिनसे करोड़ों लोगों की मीराबाई की तस्वीर बनी

panels.shot: medium shot of Mira before a small group of low-status devotees, warm and unguarded
panels.action: Mirabai sits on the temple floor among leather-workers and humble women, sharing food from a common plate, her face open and smiling.

dialogue.text: These later tales carry a clear social message: Mira as a noblewoman who chose the company of those her clan called low, and made devotion outrank birth.

i18n.hi: इन बाद की कहानियों में साफ़ सामाजिक संदेश है: मीरा एक कुलीन स्त्री, जिसने उन लोगों का साथ चुना जिन्हें उसका कुल नीचा कहता था, और भक्ति को जन्म से ऊपर कर दिया

panels.shot: wide shot of a road leading away from fort walls into open countryside
panels.action: Mirabai walks along a dusty road away from looming fort ramparts, veena slung over her shoulder, two female companions behind her, with distant temple spires ahead.

dialogue.text: Some traditions send her from Mewar to Vrindavan, others onward to Dwarka. The dates clash; the routes blur. But all agree: she moved beyond her in-laws’ fortress.

i18n.hi: कुछ परंपराएँ उसे मेवाड़ से वृंदावन भेजती हैं, कुछ आगे द्वारका तक। तारीख़ें टकराती हैं, रास्ते धुँधले हैं। पर सब मानते हैं: वो ससुराल के क़िले से बाहर निकल गई

panels.shot: atmospheric wide shot of Vrindavan-like groves and temples at dawn
panels.action: Mirabai stands in a grove beside a Yamuna-like river, with early temples rising nearby; cowherds and mendicants walk by as she gazes toward the shrine.

dialogue.text: In north Indian memory, her name settles especially in Vrindavan—among Krishna’s groves, where wandering Vaishnavas kept alive stories of a woman who sang as she renounced court life.

i18n.hi: उत्तर भारत की याद में उसका नाम ख़ास तौर पर वृंदावन में जमता है—कृष्ण के उपवनों में, जहाँ घूमते वैष्णवों ने उस स्त्री की बातों को जिंदा रखा जो दरबार छोड़कर गाते हुए चली गई

panels.shot: slow push-in on an old temple wall with a modest inscription, Mira’s devotees nearby
panels.action: Devotees touch the wall of a modest temple complex at Fatehpur, where an inscription stone is embedded; Mirabai’s figure is shown seated nearby, as if in remembered presence.

dialogue.text: By 1623, an inscription at Fatehpur shows Mira’s memory rooted in stone. What began as private defiance had become a public, enduring name in Krishna’s world.

i18n.hi: 1623 तक, फतेहपुर की एक शिला-लेख में मीरा की याद पत्थर में जम जाती है। जो कभी निजी अवज्ञा थी, वो कृष्ण-लोक में सार्वजनिक, टिकाऊ नाम बन चुकी थी

panels.shot: intimate close-up of a manuscript page of a Mira bhajan, with a hand hovering over the text
panels.action: A scholar’s hand today hovers over a page of Devanagari verses attributed to Mira, some marked, some crossed, with Mirabai’s imagined silhouette singing faintly in the background.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars sift hundreds of attributed songs, marking only a fraction as likely hers. They listen for a consistent voice beneath centuries of additions and borrowings.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान सैकड़ों माने हुए गीतों को छाँटते हैं, उनमें से बस कुछ को उसका मानते हैं। सदियों के जोड़-घटाव के नीचे एक लगातार आवाज़ खोजते हैं

panels.shot: medium shot of a present-day women’s satsang, with Mira’s image on a small calendar
panels.action: In a modern Rajasthani courtyard, women of different ages sit in a satsang circle singing; a small printed image of Mirabai with veena hangs on the wall behind them.

dialogue.text: In today’s Rajasthan, Rajput women still turn to Mira’s story to think about choice, duty, and devotion—reading her as one who walked a narrow ledge between clan and God.

i18n.hi: आज के राजस्थान में राजपूत औरतें अब भी मीरा की कहानी में अपना चुनाव, फ़र्ज़ और भक्ति सोचती हैं—उसे उस शख़्स की तरह पढ़ती हैं जो कुल और भगवान के बीच तंग धार पर चली

panels.shot: final slow pull-back from Mira singing alone in a darkened temple, light on the deity
panels.action: Mirabai sits alone in a dim temple, veena in hand, facing a lit Krishna murti; as we pull back, the temple merges into a vast starry sky.

dialogue.text: We cannot trace every step of Mirabai’s life, but the songs and stories of her refusal to vanish as a widow still echo wherever people ask how courage sounds when records fall silent.

i18n.hi: हम मीराबाई की हर क़दम नहीं पकड़ सकते, पर उसकी विधवा होकर गुम न होने की गीतों-कहानियों वाली जिद आज भी गूँजती है, जहाँ लोग पूछते हैं: जब दस्तावेज़ चुप हो जाएँ, तो हिम्मत कैसी सुनाई देती है

title_i18n.hi: मीराबाई ने विधवा की ख़ामोशी ठुकराई

subtitle_i18n.en: A Rajput widow walks out of the fort and into song
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक राजपूत विधवा किले से निकलती है, गाने में खो जाती है
